description: Local, offline policy used by the license-audit gate. It is data, not legal advice: replace the rule table with the rules your legal team has actually signed off on.

cc0-1.0.notes: Public-domain dedication; keep provenance for auditability.

cc-by-4.0.notes: Attribution required in credits and in the delivery README.

cc-by-sa-4.0.notes: Derivative assets inherit the same license; check before mixing with proprietary work.

cc-by-nc-4.0.notes: Non-commercial only: block on paid productions.

mit.notes: Code license: keep the copyright notice in the bundled add-on.

gpl-3.0.notes: Applies to Blender itself; bundling is allowed, keep sources available on the same media.

apache-2.0.notes: Include NOTICE file and patent grant text.

royalty-free-stock.notes: Stock assets stay inside the production; do not ship source files.

vendor-eula.notes: Seat-locked commercial license: record seat count and offline activation plan.

proprietary-internal.notes: Created in-house; still record authorship and consent for scan/capture data.

unknown.notes: Placeholder: the audit treats this as a critical finding on purpose.

rights_rules: A license must be recorded for every imported model, texture, HDRI, brush, groom, mocap clip and neural model.
AI training permission is a separate flag from commercial use; never infer it.
Performer capture requires a consent record even when the mesh license permits commercial use.
Redistribution of source files is blocked for stock and vendor licenses; deliver renders only.
Keep the license text and version string with the asset, not only the license name.
